Issued at 338 AM EST Sun Nov 1 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Amplified but messy pattern across the CONUS attm. Broad ridging 
over the bulk of the CONUS muddied by a bit of energy tracking ENE 
into the Mid MS Valley with a plume of Gulf moisture along/ahead of 
it across the Upper Midwest, with deeper moisture trying to creep 
into the Upper Great Lakes amid a weak warm advection regime (GRB's 
0z/01 sounding with an anomalous pwat of 1.13in vs our somewhat 
above normal 0.61in...and +8C air at 850mb creeping in from the 
west). Best warm advection, though, remains to our north across 
central/eastern Canada with more progressive northern stream (zonal 
850mb jet around 40kts)...and to our south in the Mid MS Valley, 
attendant to aforementioned muddying and negatively tilted energy, 
which is driving some deeper convection in TN/MS as of 4z...though 
there is a southerly LLJ over the central Plains. Upstream, potent 
upper level jet traversing the flow from E Asia across the 
Pacific...and cutoff energy along the West Coast starting to sharpen 
up as a 120+kt upper jet exits the base of the trough over 
SoCal...with abundant Pacific moisture transport into the SW US with 
broad low pressure west of the MS River; surface boundary stretches 
from northern CA eastward to the Dakotas. 1034mb surface high over 
the Mid-Atlantic/New England, with surface ridging still hanging 
onto our weather...for now. A few showers have made it to the 
ground, though...with a bit of wet pavement at 4z and again at 7z. 

Energy over the Mid MS Valley to continue to trek through the 
flow...crossing our area today as longwave ridge axis otherwise 
builds overhead. Troughing out west will be on the move given 
Pacific energy shoving it along...resulting in amplified troughing 
plowing into the central US early this week. This will drive surface 
pressure falls across the MS Valley...and these appear to stick 
around for a while as the upper troughing tries to get cutoff from 
the flow over the Midwest/MS Valley. Strong jet in East Asia/Pacific 
to keep sending energy eastward into North America through the 
period...which suggests a progressive but messy pattern ahead for 
the CONUS. Quite a bit of uncertainty in how this will evolve...but 
there are some signals troughing could broadly try to hang on over 
the area going into the second week of November, though perhaps not 
overly cold troughing. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Rain chances linger today, especially north...Mid-level moisture 
streams northward overhead today, and suspect this will keep skies a 
bit on the cloudy side overall. Best low-level moisture plume will 
continue to reside over the UP where there is better theta-e 
advection in the low-levels, and will be slightly closer to northern 
stream energy tracking nearby over Ontario this morning into early 
afternoon. Otherwise, not much in the way of forcing with high 
pressure still holding on. What's left of the PV max as it becomes 
embedded in the flow will track across the area later Sunday, and 
would not be entirely surprised if this helped squeeze out a few 
sprinkles/showers over the area during the late 
afternoon/evening...but think most areas will stay quiet.

Rain chances return Monday and beyond, potentially heavy at times? 
Warm advection looks to ramp back up Monday afternoon, particularly 
to our west as that trough axis enters the Central Plains and drives 
strong surface pressure falls out there as well...resulting in 
strengthening southerly flow up through the MS Valley. Expect 
increasing moisture through the column, particularly Monday night 
into Tuesday as the LLJ takes its aim on the Upper Great Lakes. 
Pwats likely jump up around or above 1.5in, which is +4-5 standard 
deviations above the mean (i.e., highly anomalous). Combined with 
the sharp trough and jet max to aid in synoptic forcing as a warm 
front lifts into the area...definitely have concerns for heavy 
rainfall during this timeframe. Not impossible the heaviest rain may 
remain focused just to our west over the central UP, a little closer 
to the PV maxima and better forcing...but certainly something that 
will need to be monitored going forward, particularly noting that 
the upper trough may be slow to move out, and could keep the threat 
of active weather (i.e., heavy rain) in the region through at least 
midweek. Noting signals for a deformation axis to hang out in the 
area into the latter half of the week, especially if the trough 
closes off into an upper low in our vicinity...think some portion of 
the Upper Great Lakes/Midwest could end up with quite a bit of rain 
by the time the week is all said and done. Attm...appears the best 
shot for multiple rounds of rain to add up will be across the Yoop, 
where the rain is rather desperately needed. Here, probabilistic 
guidance suggests rainfall totals Monday night through Tuesday could 
exceed an inch...though probabilities are much higher across the 
Upper MS Valley.
